turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Hi Mr Tan, how are you feeling now after the surgery? Let me check on you.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I’m okay lah, Doctor. Leg is numb but I feel some pain when I move a bit.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Maybe 4 or 5? Not too bad, but I can feel it there.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Alright. Have you felt any nausea or vomiting since waking up?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No vomiting, but my stomach feels a bit funny. And I’m very thirsty, Doctor.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Noted. Are you feeling comfortable with your breathing? Any shortness of breath or chest tightness?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Breathing is fine, no problem. But my back feels a bit sore from lying down too long.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good to hear. Do you remember anything during the surgery? Any sounds or feelings?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I think I heard some voices, but it was like a dream. Not very clear, Doctor.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Any other issues, like dizziness or unusual symptoms linked to your blood pressure or sugar levels?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No dizziness, but my legs feel heavy. And I’m worried about my blood sugar, lah. Can I have water soon?

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: We’ll monitor your sugar closely and give you sips of water soon. The heaviness in your legs is normal after spinal anesthesia. Rest well, Mr Tan.
